abstract: This paper considers the problem of classifying voice-band data, facsimile, and speech signals, using discriminant functions that are extensions of those described by Benvenuto (see IEEE Trans. on Commun., vol.41, no.4, p.539, 1993). Both the central second-order moment of the rectified signal, and the low order lags of the estimated autocorrelation sequence are computed. These discriminants are used to perform classification in 128 ms. with 0% misclassification for most signal types considered. Algorithm enhancements improve classification performance, reduce computational complexity, and extend the voice-band data subclassification abilities.

articleTitle: Applications of artificial neural networks to the identification of dynamical systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings 1995 Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: This paper presents two types of artificial neural network (ANN) for application to the identification of dynamical systems. The first pertains to the family of feedforward neural networks with temporal recurrent elements added to the neurons. This structure allows memory neuron networks to identify systems without having to feed past inputs and outputs explicitly. The second ANN is recurrent Its architecture looks like a discrete state-space system with a sigmoidal function in the recurrent loop. The main attraction of this three-layer recurrent neural network is its simplicity of use and the faster speed of convergence of the learning phase. The two ANNs have been tested on two dynamical systems, a fifth-order discrete theoretical plant with many multiplications between internal states in order to introduce nonlinearities, and a nonlinear transfer function from the terminal voltage to the magnetizing flux in a power transformer The challenge the ANNs is to catch the ferroresonance phenomenon as seen from the primary of the set-up transformer after a fault. The performance of these ANNs is discussed in light of various aspects of their utilisation. The comparison is based on important points such as difficulties of use, their speed and ability to converge, and their ability to generalize the behaviour of the system to inputs not available for training.

articleTitle: Alternative manipulation strategies in a virtual reality training system
publicationTitle: Proceedings 1995 Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: The importance of training simulators in the power industry has been recognised due to the risks involved for a professional in this field. However more work is needed on the training user interface. The virtual reality (VR) training simulator ESOPE-VR has been developed as a functional VR system which serves as an extension to the traditional simulator. Many issues were confronted during this development. One major issue is the man-machine strategy and interface to be used. This issue is critical since it influences the level of immersion or realism that can be achieved. This paper discusses three different hand controlled manipulation devices, their integration and some test data showing the effectiveness of their manipulation strategies.

articleTitle: Measuring the interaction complexity of teleoperated systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings 1995 Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: Concerns control of telescience systems in space by ground-based scientists, as in the Canadian Advanced Protein Crystallization Apparatus (CAPCA). We describe in this report how the formal modelling and analysis of the operator-system interaction makes it possible to evaluate the "error-proneness" of the operator interface in terms of the definition and measurement of metrics related to the complexity of the operator decisions since reduced complexity often means improved reliability. The intent is to be able to compare alternative interfaces to the very same telescience infrastructure in terms of cognitive complexity (and therefore error-proneness) by carefully evaluating the operator decision-making interactions with the system in meaningful ways. As a result, our report concludes by defining candidate complexity metrics and by discussing how they might be validated by experimental work.

articleTitle: Strategies of speed-up of the processes of search for limits of transmit and safety
publicationTitle: Proceedings 1995 Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: This article sets out the concept of three strategies which, based on the idea of voltage transient response signal energy and that of parallel running of several processors, enable a transit limit to be obtained with a margin of error of 1% in the time taken to perform one or two simulations in transient stability. The effectiveness of these strategies is demonstrated from the results of tests on the Hydro-Quebec 1991 network.

articleTitle: Comparative study of various analytical criteria for the estimation of stability limits
publicationTitle: Proceedings 1995 Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: This article compares the precision of the values of limits obtained from the signal energy of various electrical quantities such as frequency, phase angle, active and reactive power, besides the voltage modulus, at different places on a validated model of the Hydro-Quebec 1991 network. It is concluded that the signal energy of the voltage modulus gives a better estimate of the transit limits than the other electric variables.

articleTitle: Modelling by generalised equivalent circuits and identification of electric machines over an extended frequency domain
publicationTitle: Proceedings 1995 Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: This article presents the current state of research in the area of modelling of the dynamic behaviour of AC machines over an extended passband. The need to develop such models is evidenced in the area of transmission networks and that of the design and control of motors with electronic commutation. The structure, identification and implementation of specific models are presented, together with the results obtained on various devices in different fields of application. The prospects of development of research in the area are shown, and in particular, taking into account the saturation and the use of experimentation simulated by calculation of fields.
